method: Full source and call/control/data-flow review; atomscan and cleave facts including literal/decoded/flow surfaces; isolated mocked effects; forager recovery attempts; original-rule and corrected-rule controls; exact and ancestor consumer audit. No original specimen was executed against live services. No encoded or embedded executable layer or archive member exists in these three source inputs.

samples.behavior: main reads comma-separated ACCOUNTS and CANDIDATES plus CLIENT_ID from the environment. Password is the outer range and account the inner range; each pair is placed in one url.Values form with password grant_type and Graph default scope and submitted through http.PostForm to Microsoft organizations OAuth v2 token endpoint. Responses are closed without reading status, tokens or success results. No delay, lockout avoidance, credential harvesting, token exfiltration, persistence or payload execution is implemented. Spanish identifiers are ordinary names, not obfuscation. Mocked PostForm confirmed four submissions in password-major order without network access.
samples.balance_of_evidence: MALICIOUS on balance: the only application behavior is a Cartesian sweep of candidate passwords across accounts against a real remote authentication service, rather than ordinary single-account OAuth login. Authorized tenant auditing is possible, but no authorization, test harness or audit deployment context accompanies this standalone main. The precise spray detector is accurate even though ML remains benign.

samples.identity: Incomplete Excel VBA XLM/Regsvr32 command stager
samples.behavior: This is exported Excel VBA, not a working WSH VBScript despite its extension: Attribute VB_Name, Declare Function and Excel globals require a VBA host. Auto_Open suppresses errors, adds an international XLM macro sheet, hides the named sheet, writes a regsvr32 -silent relative-path command as plain text in I17, and asks Application.Run to run H1. No H1 or EXEC/REGISTER formula is populated. URLDownloadToFile is a declared binding, never invoked; there is no download URL, write-to-disk operation or native registration call. The -silent token is not evidence of successful regsvr32 argument handling. Missing workbook/formulas and runtime success are not invented.
samples.balance_of_evidence: MALICIOUS on balance as an incomplete attack fragment: hidden XLM setup, staged regsvr32 command and auto-open/macro-run request form a concealed native-command staging attempt. Its nonfunctional isolated packaging limits execution claims, not the evidence of attack-oriented construction. A security training corpus or analyst reproduction could explain possession; no such enclosing deployment context was supplied. The repository contains a byte-identical attack fixture, which is not independent corroboration or family attribution.

samples.behavior: The zsh script clears all extended attributes on its first argument, fetches a public iCloud calendar to a hidden /tmp ICS file and pipes that same file through cat into zsh -s. Independently, the later literal commands fetch a URL ending stage2.enc to a hidden gzip-tar path, extract into /tmp, recursively clear attributes on a hidden app, force/deep ad-hoc sign it and open the same app. There is no decryption despite the .enc URL, no persistence, cleanup, exfiltration or privilege escalation. The source comments describe an inspired reconstruction; they do not prove MacSync identity or the content of the missing calendar. xattr -c clears quarantine only if present; ad-hoc signing does not prove Gatekeeper/notarization acceptance. All shell effects were captured with command stubs; none contacted a service or altered a real app.
samples.balance_of_evidence: MALICIOUS on balance: interpreting downloaded calendar data as shell commands, followed by hidden application staging and trust-metadata/signature modification, is attack-oriented delivery beyond calendar synchronization. The supplied source is a demonstration/reconstruction rather than corroborated family attribution. No authorized research or installation context is supplied. Runtime payload success remains unknown.
